note: Generated by `npm run claude-plugin` from the Riva Sai API schema. Do not edit.

fences.add.description: Adds a fence through points (closed joins the last point to the first).

fences.list.description: Lists fences, hedges and low walls on the site.

floors.add.description: Adds a floor (optionally copying walls/content from another, and activating it).

floors.remove.description: Removes a floor and its content.

floors.update.description: Updates a floor name, elevation or height.

items.add.description: Places a catalog item (dims/elevation default from the catalog).

items.facing.description: Which way an item faces: nearest compass point (plan up is north), degrees clockwise from north and the front vector; null for items without a front (round tables, plants, rugs, ceiling lights).

landscape.add.description: Adds a landscape area from a polygon; elevation and finish default per kind.

landscape.kinds.description: Landscape area kinds with their default name, material, elevation and water depth.

landscape.list.description: Lists landscape areas (lawns, patios, driveways, paths, beds, pools, ponds, gravel, decks, sand).

landscape.stats.description: Area, perimeter and centroid of a landscape area.

landscape.update.description: Updates a landscape area (null material restores the kind default).

openings.add.description: Adds a door/window/opening to a wall: give wallId (+ offset, cm from wall.a to the centre; default the middle) or at, the centre point on the plan (the nearest wall within 30 cm is used). opensInto (a room id) makes a door swing into that room.

project.setPhase.description: Sets the renovation phase of walls, openings and items as one undo step: ids names them, all: true marks every wall, opening and item on every floor. Start a renovation by marking all 'existing', then set 'demolish' on what goes and add new work. Returns the changed ids and whether the project is a renovation.

roofStyles.add.description: Adds a styled roof over a building: by default the largest building of the top storey with walls (or the building containing 'at', or an explicit wall-line 'outline'). The outline is the exterior face of the exterior walls; eaves = outline + overhang. Defaults per style (pitch, overhang, material): see roofStyles.styles(). With replaceCoreRoofs (default true) the core roofs (roofs.*) of that storey whose centre lies under the new roof are removed so they do not overlap. One undo step. Returns the stored roof (StyledRoof). Example: { "options": { "style": "gambrel", "rise": 12 } }, { "options": { "style": "flat", "params": { "parapet": 60 } } }. Units: cm for lengths/heights, degrees for pitches (rise x:12 = inches per 12 of run, pitch = atan(rise / 12)); plan x right, y down.

roofStyles.addDormer.description: Adds a dormer (gable, shed, hip or eyebrow) on a sloped plane of a styled roof. 'at' is the plan point (cm) where the dormer front stands; the dormer extends upslope from it. It must lie on a pitched plane of a style that supports dormers (not flat, butterfly, sawtooth, clerestory, curved or conical), fully inside that plane, below the ridge and >= 30 cm from hips, valleys, rakes and other dormers — otherwise INVALID_ARGUMENT explains why. Defaults: width 120 cm, front height 110 cm, pitch from the host slope. One undo step. Returns the dormer. Example: { "options": { "roofId": "sroof1", "type": "gable", "at": { "x": 300, "y": 620 } } }. Units: cm for lengths/heights, degrees for pitches (rise x:12 = inches per 12 of run, pitch = atan(rise / 12)); plan x right, y down.

roofStyles.adopt.description: Converts a core roof (roofs.list / floor.roofs, types gable, hip, shed, flat) into a styled roof of the same storey, keeping its outline (eave polygon minus the overhang), pitch, overhang, ridge angle, base height and material, then removes the core roof. style defaults to the core type (e.g. 'hip'); pass any style to restyle it (e.g. 'mansard'). One undo step. Returns the new StyledRoof.

roofStyles.check.description: Checks styled roofs (one with id, else all) against roofing codes and guidance: covering minimum slopes (IRC R905: asphalt shingles >= 2:12 with double underlayment up to 4:12, clay/concrete tile >= 2.5:12, slate >= 4:12, wood shingles >= 3:12, standing-seam metal >= 0.25:12, membranes 0.25:12-2:12), drainage of flat / butterfly / valley roofs, snow and wind guidance (pass climate), sawtooth glazing orientation (should face away from the equator; site.sun.latitude), footprint fit (pyramid / dome / conical on elongated outlines), extreme pitches and heights, dormers that no longer fit. Returns issues [{ severity error|warning|info, code, message, reference, roofId }]. Read-only.

roofStyles.describe.description: AI-oriented summary of the styled roofs: a text with each roof (style, storey, pitch in degrees and x:12, covering, overhang, eave / ridge heights in cm, areas in m², dormers, issue counts) and suggested next steps, plus a per-roof summary list. Read-only.

roofStyles.geometry.description: Returns the computed 3D geometry of a styled roof: planar faces (kind slope|flat|gable|wall|glazing|fascia|soffit, vertices counter-clockwise from outside, outward unit normal, dormer id), roof-plan lines (ridge, hip, valley, eave, rake, break, apex), the eave outline and eaveHeight / ridgeHeight. Coordinates: plan x/y in cm, z in cm above the storey base (world height = storey elevation + z). Read-only. Units: cm for lengths/heights, degrees for pitches (rise x:12 = inches per 12 of run, pitch = atan(rise / 12)); plan x right, y down.

roofStyles.get.description: Returns one styled roof by id (outline cm, pitch degrees, overhang cm, params, dormers). Read-only; NOT_FOUND for unknown ids.

roofStyles.list.description: Lists the styled roofs of the project (or of one storey) with their stored settings (outline cm, pitch degrees, overhang cm, params, dormers). Read-only.

roofStyles.metrics.description: Quantities of a styled roof for take-off: style, pitch (degrees), rise (x:12), eaveHeight / ridgeHeight (cm above the storey base), roofHeight (ridge above the wall-line base, cm), footprintM2 (eave outline), roofAreaM2 (slope + flat faces), facesByKind, ridgeLength / hipLength / valleyLength / eaveLength / rakeLength / breakLength (cm), gableAreaM2, glazingAreaM2 and atticVolumeM3 (volume under the roof above the wall-line base). Read-only.

roofStyles.recommend.description: Ranks roof styles for a building outline (default: the largest building on the top storey with walls), a climate, an architectural style (free text such as 'Dutch Colonial', 'Craftsman', 'modern', 'barn'), a required covering and the wish for a usable attic. Returns the classified footprint {shape: rectangle|square|l-shape|t-shape|u-shape|round|irregular, width, depth (cm, oriented bounding box), areaM2} and recommendations sorted by score (0..1), each with pitch (degrees), rise (x:12), params, material, overhang (cm), reasons and cautions — ready to pass to roofStyles.add. Read-only. Units: cm for lengths/heights, degrees for pitches (rise x:12 = inches per 12 of run, pitch = atan(rise / 12)); plan x right, y down.

roofStyles.remove.description: Removes a styled roof (with its dormers). One undo step. Returns { removed: true, id }.

roofStyles.removeDormer.description: Removes a dormer from a styled roof. One undo step. Returns { removed: true, roofId, dormerId }.

roofStyles.styles.description: Lists the 20 roof styles the plugin models with what an architect needs to choose one: id, name, aliases (e.g. 'barn roof', 'skillion', 'north light'), description, typicalPitch {min, max, default} in degrees and the same range as rise (x:12), the params it uses, suited footprints, climate notes, architectural styles (e.g. 'Dutch Colonial', 'Second Empire', 'Cape Cod'), suitable coverings (catalog material ids, defaultMaterial first) and the covering minimum-slope notes, whether it supports dormers. Units: cm for lengths/heights, degrees for pitches (rise x:12 = inches per 12 of run, pitch = atan(rise / 12)); plan x right, y down.

roofStyles.update.description: Changes a styled roof: style, outline, pitch (degrees) or rise (x:12), overhang (cm), ridgeAngle (radians), baseHeight (cm), material, params (merged into the current params; a null value removes a key) or name. Dormers are kept (check() reports any that no longer fit). One undo step. Returns the updated roof. Example: { "options": { "id": "sroof1", "changes": { "style": "hip", "rise": 6 } } }. Units: cm for lengths/heights, degrees for pitches (rise x:12 = inches per 12 of run, pitch = atan(rise / 12)); plan x right, y down.

roofs.add.description: Adds a roof over an eave outline (defaults: gable, 30°, no overhang, ridge along the longest side).

roofs.auto.description: Roofs the building(s) of a floor from the exterior wall outline (offset by half the wall thickness plus overhang, default 30 cm); `at` picks one building; existing roofs over it are replaced unless replace=false.

roofs.geometry.description: 3D faces of a roof (slopes, gables, flat top, fascia, soffit) with heights above the floor base.

rooms.createRectangular.description: Draws a rectangular room with top-left corner x,y (wall centre lines). Neighbouring rooms share walls: a side along an existing wall reuses it (splitting it where the side ends) and only the uncovered parts get new walls. walls[] holds one wall per side - north, east, south, west (the first piece of each side); sides[] holds every wall of each side in order.

rooms.setWallFinish.description: Sets the finish of every wall face enclosing a room (null restores the default paint) as one undo step; returns the changed walls.

rooms.stats.description: Area, perimeter and centroid of a room.

rooms.wallFaces.description: Lists the wall faces enclosing a room (wall id and the side looking into the room).

site.fitBoundary.description: Sets the lot boundary to a rectangle around everything on the plan plus a margin (cm, default 500), snapped outwards to 50 cm.

site.get.description: Returns the site: lot boundary, ground material, landscape areas, fences, sun and sky.

site.setSunTime.description: Places the sun for a local solar time (hours, 12 = noon), latitude (degrees; default the site's stored latitude, else 45; stored as site.sun.latitude) and day of the year (default 172, the June solstice).

site.sunTime.description: The local solar time (hours) matching the current sun for a latitude (default the site latitude, else 45) and day of the year (default 172), or null when the sun was placed another way.

site.update.description: Updates the lot boundary (null = unbounded), ground material, sun position (partial) or sky.

storeys.addBasement.description: Adds a storey below the lowest one: elevation = lowest.elevation - height (negative elevations are below ground level). Copies the exterior walls of the lowest storey by default. One undo step. Returns the new floor.

storeys.addStairs.description: Places a straight staircase (catalog item stairs-straight, 100 cm wide, about 107 cm of run per metre of rise) on a storey, climbing to the storey directly above; its slab opening and guard rails above are created automatically. The storey above must start where this one ends (within 30 cm). Without a position it is placed along an exterior wall where it fits clear of walls on both storeys, furniture and the stairwell coming up from below; fails with CONFLICT if nothing fits (then pass position). One undo step. Returns the staircase item.

storeys.addStorey.description: Adds a storey directly on top of another one (default: the top storey): its elevation is from.elevation + from.height. Copies the outline of the storey below by default so the new storey has exterior walls and a detected room. If storeys already sit at or above that elevation they are raised by the new height (inserting a storey). When the new storey becomes the top one, the roofs of the storey below move up onto it (moveRoofs). One undo step. Returns the new floor.

storeys.fromFootprint.description: Builds a complete multi-storey shell from a footprint polygon: on each storey closed exterior walls along the polygon (wall center lines), a detected room named after the storey, a straight staircase on every storey except the top one (placed inside along an exterior wall, clear of walls and of the stairwell below), and a roof on the top storey. Storeys are stacked from ground level 0 with conventional names. If every existing floor is empty (a new project) they are reused/removed; otherwise the new storeys are built on top of the existing building unless replace is true (which removes all existing floors and their content). Makes the ground storey active. One undo step. Returns { floors, roofs }. Example: a 10 x 8 m house = polygon [{x:0,y:0},{x:1000,y:0},{x:1000,y:800},{x:0,y:800}].

storeys.renumber.description: Renames all storeys by elevation with conventional names: storeys below ground level (elevation < 0) are 'Basement', 'Basement 2', ... (deeper ones get higher numbers); the lowest storey at or above 0 is 'Ground floor', then '1st floor', '2nd floor', '3rd floor', '4th floor', ... One undo step (none if nothing changes). Returns the floors bottom to top.

storeys.stack.description: Adds `count` storeys on top of the building, one above the other (each like storeys.addStorey on the current top storey, copying from the storey just below it). Roofs move up to the new top. One undo step for the whole stack. Returns the new floors, bottom to top.

storeys.summary.description: Storey-by-storey overview of the building, bottom to top. For each floor: id, name, level (0 = ground floor, 1 = first floor above it, -1 = basement), elevation and height and top (elevation + height) in cm, counts of walls/rooms/items/roofs, grossAreaM2 (area inside the exterior outline measured to the outer wall faces, m²), roomAreaM2 (sum of room polygons, m²), stairsUp / stairsDown (a staircase connects it to the storey above / below), active. Plus totals, lowestElevation (cm), buildingHeight (highest storey top or roof ridge above ground level 0, cm) and totalHeight (from the lowest storey base, cm). Read-only; call it first to understand the building.

storeys.validate.description: Checks the storey stack and returns issues (empty array = all good), bottom to top. Codes: ELEVATION_OVERLAP (error: a storey starts below the top of the one under it), ELEVATION_GAP (warning: space between storeys, cm), UNSUPPORTED_OVERHANG (warning: an upper storey outline extends beyond the outer wall faces of the storey below, details.areaM2), NO_STAIRS (warning: two consecutive storeys with content but no staircase between them), STAIRS_TO_NOWHERE (warning: a staircase does not reach a storey above), LOW_HEADROOM (warning: storey height below 220 cm), TALL_STOREY (warning: above 450 cm), OPEN_ENVELOPE (warning: walls but no closed exterior outline), ROOF_UNDER_STOREY (warning: a roof is covered by a storey above), NO_ROOF (info: the top storey has a closed outline but no roof), EMPTY_FLOOR (info). Read-only.

terrain.addBreakline.description: Adds a breakline: a 3D polyline the existing ground follows between its vertices (kerbs, ridge lines, top / toe of banks, ditch flow lines, retaining-wall tops). The TIN is made conforming (breakline segments become triangle edges, even with survey shots a few cm beside them), so the TIN follows it exactly; the raster surfaces sample it at the grid resolution, so a sharp break is rounded over one grid cell. Parts far outside the terrain extent are ignored. 'hard' = a sharp grade break (densified every resolution / 2), 'soft' = a guide line (every resolution). Plan coordinates in cm: x to the right, y downwards on the plan (north is up, i.e. -y). Elevations z in cm above the project datum: 0 = base of the ground floor; the app draws flat ground at -1 cm. One undo step. Returns the breakline { id, points, kind }.

terrain.addPad.description: Adds a grading pad: a flat area at a finished-grade elevation (building pad, patio, parking / road bed) whose edges daylight into the existing ground with cut slopes (where the ground is higher) and fill slopes (where it is lower). Later pads win inside their own outline. Plan coordinates in cm: x to the right, y downwards on the plan (north is up, i.e. -y). Elevations z in cm above the project datum: 0 = base of the ground floor; the app draws flat ground at -1 cm. Typical pad elevations: building pad = finished floor - 15 cm (use terrain.padForBuilding), patio = floor - 2..15 cm. One undo step. Returns { pad, earthwork } with the pad's cut / fill in m³.

terrain.addPoints.description: Adds survey points (spot elevations) to the existing ground; the surface is a TIN through all points (linear between them, flat beyond the outermost ones). Plan coordinates in cm: x to the right, y downwards on the plan (north is up, i.e. -y). Elevations z in cm above the project datum: 0 = base of the ground floor; the app draws flat ground at -1 cm. Max 20000 points in total. One undo step. Returns { added, total, ids }.

terrain.analyze.description: Site analysis: terrain extent, elevation statistics of the existing and proposed surfaces (cm), slope histogram of the chosen surface in the civil slope classes 0-2 / 2-5 / 5-10 / 10-15 / 15-25 / 25-33 / 33-50 / >50 % (area m² and share %), mean / max slope (%) and where the steepest cell is, and earthwork between existing and proposed: cut, fill, net (fill - cut; > 0 = import soil) and total in m³, balance ratio, disturbed area m², per pad. Read-only.

terrain.check.description: Site-engineering code checks of the graded terrain; returns issues ordered error, warning, info (empty = all good). Codes: drainage-fall (IRC R401.3: ground must fall >= 15.2 cm / 6 in within 3.05 m / 10 ft of the foundation, 2 % on paving; error when it slopes toward the house), floor-below-grade (error), foundation-clearance (IRC R404.1.6: >= 15.2 cm above grade), slope-over-50 (IBC J106/J107: steeper than 2H:1V needs a retaining wall), slope-over-33 (not mowable), path-ramp-max (ADA 405.2: > 8.33 %), path-running-slope (ADA 403.3: > 5 % is a ramp), path-cross-slope (> 2.08 %), driveway-slope (> 15 %; both per leg, on the design ground), pad-step (pads meet with a > 2 cm step), pool-on-slope (existing ground > 10 %), grading-beyond-lot (IBC J108: slopes reach neighbouring land), grading-truncated (slopes leave the terrain extent), earthwork-unbalanced (net > 20 % of the total). Read-only.

terrain.clear.description: Removes all terrain data from the project (back to the flat ground). One undo step. Returns { removed } (false when there was none).

terrain.contours.description: Contour lines of the existing or proposed surface: polylines (plan cm, simplified) at multiples of the interval (cm); major (index) lines every settings.majorEvery levels. Read-only. Returns { surface, interval (cm, may be coarser than asked when there would be too many levels), count, truncated, lines: [{ elevation (cm), major, closed, points }] }.

terrain.describe.description: Compact site summary for an AI agent: a short text plus numbers — terrain extent (m), point / breakline / pad counts, existing and proposed elevation ranges (cm), mean slope, area per slope class, the steepest areas, every pad with its elevation and cut / fill, the earthwork balance, issue counts with the top issues, and suggested next steps (which terrain.* call to make). Read-only; call it first and after each change.

terrain.elevationAt.description: Elevations (cm) of the existing or proposed surface at plan points (cm), bilinear on the surface grid; null for points outside the terrain extent. Plan coordinates in cm: x to the right, y downwards on the plan (north is up, i.e. -y). Elevations z in cm above the project datum: 0 = base of the ground floor; the app draws flat ground at -1 cm. Read-only. Returns an array of numbers / null in the order of the points.

terrain.generate.description: Creates the existing ground (EG) from a procedural preset, replacing all survey points and breaklines (pads, boundary and settings are kept unless keepPads is false). Use it for concept design when there is no survey; import a real survey with terrain.importSurvey. Presets: 'flat' (level at base), 'slope' (a plane falling grade % towards direction), 'hill' (a mound of height relief at center), 'valley' (a trough along direction, relief deep), 'ridge' (a crest along direction, relief high), 'terraced' (terraces stepping down towards direction over relief), 'rolling' (smooth random undulation of amplitude relief, varied by seed). Elevations are relative to base (default -1 cm = the app's flat ground); the house's ground floor is at 0, so a hill under a house buries it until you grade a pad (terrain.padForBuilding). Plan coordinates in cm: x to the right, y downwards on the plan (north is up, i.e. -y). Elevations z in cm above the project datum: 0 = base of the ground floor; the app draws flat ground at -1 cm. One undo step. Returns { preset, points, spacing, bounds, min, max } (elevations cm). Example: { preset: 'slope', grade: 8, direction: 1.5708 } = ground falling 8 % towards +y (towards the bottom of the plan, south).

terrain.get.description: Returns the terrain data stored in the project (survey points, breaklines, boundary, pads, settings), or null when the project has no terrain (flat ground at -1 cm). Plan coordinates in cm: x to the right, y downwards on the plan (north is up, i.e. -y). Elevations z in cm above the project datum: 0 = base of the ground floor; the app draws flat ground at -1 cm. Read-only. For an overview use terrain.describe instead (the point list can be large).

terrain.importSurvey.description: Imports survey points from CSV / TSV / whitespace text as exported by total stations and civil software. Columns by format: PNEZD = point, northing, easting, elevation, description; PENZD / PXYZD = point, easting, northing, elevation, description; XYZ / ENZ = easting, northing, elevation; NEZ = northing, easting, elevation. Header, blank and comment lines (# // ;) are skipped; bad lines are reported, not fatal. Easting becomes plan x and northing plan -y (north up). Use origin to bring large grid coordinates near the plan origin, and always give elevationDatum (the survey level of the finished ground floor, file units) for real surveys: z = 0 is the ground floor, so absolute elevations (e.g. 251 m) bury the house. One undo step. Returns { imported, total, skipped, errors: [{line, message, text}] (first 50), errorCount, origin, warnings } (warnings: e.g. imported ground far from the floor level, with a suggested elevationDatum).

terrain.padForBuilding.description: Grades a building pad for every building (closed exterior wall outline) of a storey standing on the ground: the outline at the outer wall faces grown by offset (apron around the foundation), at elevation at the walls (default: floor elevation - 15 cm, the 6 in foundation clearance of IRC R404.1.6) falling away from them at fall % (default 5, IRC R401.3), with 2:1 cut and 3:1 fill side slopes. Ids 'building-1', 'building-2'...; replaced when called again. Where the ground all round is higher than the pad (a pit, e.g. flat ground at -1 cm with the floor at 0) water runs toward the house and terrain.check reports drainage-fall: warnings then says how high the finished floor must be (adjacent ground + 15.24 cm clearance + 15.24 cm fall); raise it (floors.update) and call this again. One undo step. Returns { pads, earthwork (m³ per pad), warnings }.

terrain.removeBreakline.description: Removes a breakline by id. One undo step. Returns { removed: true }; NOT_FOUND for an unknown id.

terrain.removePad.description: Removes a pad by id. One undo step. Returns { removed: true }; NOT_FOUND for an unknown id.

terrain.removePoints.description: Removes survey points by id and/or all points inside a plan polygon (cm). Give ids, within or both (a point matching either is removed); all: true removes every point. One undo step (none when nothing matches). Returns { removed, total }.

terrain.setBoundary.description: Sets the extent of the terrain surface (plan polygon, cm), or null to use the default: the lot boundary (site.boundary), else the plan content bounds plus 5 m (grown to include all survey points). Make it larger than the lot when grading slopes must continue onto neighbouring land. One undo step. Returns { boundary } (null = default).

terrain.settings.description: Reads or changes the terrain settings (contour interval, grid resolution, site-area grading, 3D material, what the plan shows). Pass only the fields to change; with no fields it just returns the settings. Creates empty terrain data when the project has none. One undo step when something changes. Returns the settings.

terrain.updatePad.description: Changes a pad (only the given fields). One undo step. Returns { pad, earthwork }. Example: lower a pad by setting changes.elevation.

walls.add.description: Adds a wall from a to b (cm).

walls.addPolyline.description: Adds connected walls through points (closed connects back to the start).

walls.move.description: Translates walls by delta as one undo step; straight continuations move along and joined walls stretch, so rooms stay square and keep their identity.

walls.moveEndpoint.description: Moves a wall endpoint; connected walls follow unless connected=false.

walls.remove.description: Removes a wall and its openings.

walls.split.description: Splits a wall at a point or offset; returns both parts.
